page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64 and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 3990.17, and the uncached memory read bandwidth is relatively low at 37.14 GB/sec. Large-block memory writes and database operations perform in the average tier, with Passmark database operations scoring 2890.86.

Given its high memory density and local NVMe storage, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The hardware profile is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers, and text processing tasks. It is less optimal for highly parallelized compute tasks, software compilation, or large-scale language model inference due to its lower multi-core performance and memory read bandwidth constraints.
